prompt: A pump fills a tank at $4$ gallons per minute. How long to fill a $100$-gallon tank?
hint: Every minute the pump adds the same amount of water. How many of those equal amounts fit into the whole tank?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a tiny tank first: how long would this pump take to fill $8$ gallons? Use the same thinking for the $100$-gallon tank.
Every minute the pump adds the same amount of water. How many of those equal amounts fit into the whole tank?
The tank holds $100$ gallons and each minute adds $4$ gallons, so divide: work out $100 \div 4$.
$100 \div 4 = 25$, so it takes $25$ minutes to fill the tank.

explanation: The rate is $4$ gallons for each minute, so the time is the number of $4$-gallon groups in the tank.
Divide the tank size by the rate: $100 \div 4$.
The quotient is $25$, and the check $25 \times 4 = 100$ confirms it.
The pump fills the tank in $25$ minutes.
